transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist here. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I came in because... lately I've just been feeling more on edge and down than usual. My sister and her new baby moved back into the house recently, and ever since then, it's just been a lot. I find myself snapping over little stuff at home, and then by the time I get to my classes or the machine shop, I'm already completely drained. I'm still getting by, mostly, but I've missed a couple of deadlines for school. I even had to back out of helping build the set for the theater department because I just couldn't keep everything straight in my head anymore. It's just getting harder to manage.
When did you first start noticing these feelings of being on edge and down? Was it right around the time your sister and baby moved in, or had you been experiencing this before that?

No, I was actually doing okay before they moved in. Um, I didn't really have these issues before that. I'd say the trouble started within a couple of weeks of them getting settled, you know, once the house just got really crowded and loud. That's when I started noticing it.

Since this started a few weeks ago, have you experienced any sudden episodes where your heart was racing, you felt like you couldn't breathe, or you had intense fear that came on very quickly out of nowhere?

No, I haven't had anything like that. Um, my heart doesn't race out of nowhere or anything, and I can breathe fine. I don't get any sudden intense fear. It's really just... more of a constant stress and feeling irritated all the time, not like a sudden attack.

Since this started a few weeks ago, have you noticed any feeling of being disconnected from your surroundings or from yourself, like things around you don't feel real, or like you're watching yourself from outside your body?

No, nothing like that. I definitely feel like I'm in my own body, and everything around me feels real. It's just... it's just really loud and chaotic right now. I don't feel disconnected, just stressed out.
If your sister and baby weren't living with you right now, do you think you'd still be feeling this down and irritable, or do you think those feelings would go away?

I think if they weren't here, I'd probably be fine. I mean, the situation hasn't ended yet—my sister and the baby are still living with us, so it's all still happening. Everything I'm feeling is just tied to this big change at home. If that went back to normal, I think I would too.

You mentioned the trouble started within a couple of weeks of your sister moving in—so we're talking about roughly 4 weeks ago now that you're feeling this way. Is that about right, or has it been longer or shorter than that?
Yeah, that's right. It's been going on for about a month now, basically ever since my sister and the baby moved back into the house.

You mentioned missing a couple of deadlines for school and backing out of the theater set. Beyond those specific things, how much has this stress and irritability been affecting your ability to do your daily activities and responsibilities overall?

I mean, overall, I'm still going to class and showing up for work. It hasn't stopped me from doing the main things. It's really just what we talked about—turning in a couple of assignments late and having to drop out of building that community theater set. I just couldn't keep up with everything at once with how things are right now. But beyond that, I'm still getting through my regular day-to-day stuff.
Do you know how long your sister and the baby are planning to stay with your family, or is it unclear at this point?

I'm not really sure, honestly. It's kind of up in the air right now. She hasn't given a specific date or anything, so... yeah, it's pretty unclear. I guess they're just staying until she figures things out and gets back on her feet.

When your sister does move out—whether that's in a few weeks, a few months, or whenever—do you think you'd expect to feel back to normal fairly quickly, or do you think it might take you a while to recover even after the situation changes?

I think... yeah, I'd probably feel back to normal pretty quickly once they actually leave. The thing is, the situation hasn't really ended yet. My sister and her newborn are still living with us right now, so everything I'm dealing with is still just tied to that change at home. Once the house is quiet again and things go back to how they were, I expect I'll bounce right back.

You mentioned you're still getting to class and work, but I want to make sure I understand the full picture. When you think about how this stress and irritability has been affecting you overall—your sleep, your appetite, your concentration, your relationships with friends or family—would you say it's causing you significant distress, even if you're still managing to get through the day?

I mean, I wouldn't say it's significant distress. It's definitely annoying, and I'm definitely more irritable with my family right now because the house is so crowded and loud. But my sleep is fine, my appetite is normal. I'm still hanging out with my friends when I can. It's really just the frustration of the situation at home, but it's not ruining my life or anything. It's just a lot to deal with right now.

You mentioned missing a couple of deadlines and backing out of the theater set—but thinking about it more broadly, would you say this stress is making it noticeably harder for you to do well in school or at work compared to how you were doing before your sister moved in?

Well, yeah, it is noticeably harder. Like I said, I'm still showing up to class and going to my job, but I'm definitely not doing as well as I was before. I've turned in a couple of school assignments late because I just can't focus with all the noise at home. And dropping that community theater set project... I just had to, because I couldn't keep up with everything on my plate right now. So it's definitely affecting my performance, for sure.

You mentioned you're still managing work and classes, but let me ask this more directly: would you say the stress and irritability from your sister moving in has caused you real problems in your relationships, your schoolwork, or your job—problems that are more than just annoying, but actually meaningful enough that you'd want to do something about it if you could?

Yeah, I guess it has caused some real problems. Like, I'm still going to class and work, but... I've turned in a couple of assignments late, which isn't really like me. And I had to drop out of building that set for the community theater because I just couldn't keep up with everything. So, yeah, it's definitely messing with my schoolwork and the stuff I usually like doing. It's more than just annoying at this point.
